problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\frac{\sqrt{5}s}{3}⟩,\,0\le s\le 4\pi .
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡3s,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3s⟩,\,0\le s\le \frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3s)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3s,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡3s⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡3s,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3s⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡3s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{cos}⁡3s,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3s⟩ \\  & =-3⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡3s,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3s⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-3|\cdot \sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡3s+{sin}^{2}⁡3s} \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
